data: First Chinese GTO success (1984) + comsat workhorse

Fleet launch-site entry added during the cross-correlation analysis (#306 follow-up). XSC LC-3 hosted the first Long March 3 launch attempt on 1984-01-29 (partial failure, third-stage re-ignition) and the first successful flight on 1984-04-08 (first Chinese GTO success), then many subsequent Apstar / Asiasat / Sinosat missions.
First CZ-3 operational successes — DFH-2 first GTO success, Apstar / Asiasat / Sinosat era

Xichang LC-3 hosted the first Long March 3 launch attempt on January 29, 1984 (DFH-2-01), which partially failed on third-stage re-ignition. The first successful Long March 3 flight occurred on April 8, 1984 (DFH-2-02), which placed the DFH-2 'Dong Fang Hong-2' communications satellite into geostationary transfer orbit — China's first GTO success. Both CZ-3 flights were from LC-3. Through the 1990s it supported many Apstar, Asiasat, and Sinosat commercial communications launches. Today it remains in active use alongside LC-2 for Long March 3B operations.
Long March 3A/3B family — most Chinese GTO commercial launches and Beidou GNSS deployments
China's crewed-spaceflight pad — every Shenzhou crew
Long March 2D / 4B / 4C polar-orbit workhorse — Yaogan, Gaofen, weather sats
China's heavy-lift pad — Long March 5 to Tianhe, Chang'e 5/6, Tianwen-1, and the lunar return programme
Long March 7 pad on Hainan: all ten Tianzhou cargo ships to Tiangong, plus Long March 8 flights
Early Ariane pad — 1 Ariane 2, 2 Ariane 3, 116 Ariane 4 (1986-2003)
